1.explanation: Both the core BASIC highlighter (prism-basic.js/.min.js) and the VB.NET extension (prism-vbnet.js/.min.js) rely on a regular-expression that defines which characters are allowed inside a quoted string. Currently that pattern does not include the '@' character, so any string containing '@' won’t match and the opening quote is lost. To fix the bug, the string-matching regex in prism-basic.js (and its minified counterpart) must be updated to include '@', and the same change should be applied in prism-vbnet.js (and its minified file) if it overrides or extends the BASIC string pattern for VB.NET.
1.bug_scenario: In VB.NET code blocks, string literals that contain the '@' character (for example "Select * from test Where Code=@Code") are not being picked up as strings by the Prism highlighter. As a result the opening quote isn’t recognized and the rest of the line is highlighted incorrectly. Strings without '@' (e.g. "Select * from test Where Code=Code") still highlight correctly.

2.explanation: prism-basic.js defines the core BASIC string-matching regex that VB.NET ends up inheriting (or building on), but its character class doesn’t permit the “@” character, so any VB.NET string containing @ is not recognized properly. prism-vbnet.js registers the VB.NET language and either inherits that broken pattern or overrides it without adding @. To fix the bug you must update the string pattern in prism-basic.js (and rebuild its .min.js) or explicitly override it in prism-vbnet.js (and rebuild its .min.js) so that ‘@’ is allowed inside quoted strings.
